title: Calculating an array element's memory address
summary: Compute an element's location directly from the starting address, fixed element size, and index.
description: The upper part arranges the array, indices, and memory addresses with the column at index 3 highlighted; the lower part gives the address formula and a worked substitution. Each element occupies 4 bytes; the upper address row uses two-digit notation (such as 00 and 12), while the formula below uses three-digit notation (000 and 012). Leading zeros are purely for alignment, and all numbers are decimal.
result: With contiguous storage and equal-sized elements, a single multiplication and addition gives the address, supporting O(1) random access.

frames.title: Calculating an array element's memory address
frames.explanation: Element address = address of the first element + element size × index. Indexing starts at 0, so index 3 is the 4th element, with value 5; it is 3 elements past the first element, giving a byte offset of 4 × 3 = 12 and an address of 000 + 4 × 3 = 012. This locates the element by index rather than searching for an element whose value is 3.
